title: Ngā Whetū o te Tau Hou | The Stars of the New Year
location: Te Whatu Stardome | Observatory & Planetarium, 670 Manukau Rd, Maungakiekie/One Tree Hill Domain, Epsom, Auckland 1023, Auckland
description:
In this immersive planetarium experience, you’ll journey through the night sky to explore the Matariki star cluster and its importance in Aotearoa and te ao Māori.
Discover the rich pūrākau (stories), science and traditions connected to each of the nine whetū, learn about the Maramataka (the Māori lunar calendar), and reflect on how Matariki guides us through the cycles of the year along with many other significant stars.
Whether you’re reconnecting with Matariki or experiencing it for the first time, this show is a great way to honour the season and gain a deeper appreciation of Māori astronomy and our place within the cosmos.

title: The New Job Market: Hiring, Hunting, and AI in the Middle
location: 2 Freyberg Place, Auckland
description:
This session looks at how AI is reshaping every stage of the job hunt - from the CV that gets written, to the screening system that reads it, to the interview on the other side, to the market candidates are landing in.

The focus is practical and aimed at job seekers, career changers, and anyone trying to make sense of how hiring actually works now - but recruiters, hiring managers, and HR folks will get plenty out of it too.

We'll explore-

* The current challenges, specifically in the Auckland NZ marketplace
* Writing CVs and cover letters with AI - what works, what flags as generic, and how to keep your voice
* Getting past the bots - how applicant tracking systems and AI screeners actually evaluate applications
* The new interview landscape - AI-assisted screening calls, async video interviews, and live AI note-takers
* Interview prep with AI - mock interviews, company research, and rehearsing tough questions
* Where AI helps you stand out vs. where it makes everyone sound the same
* Job market shifts - which roles are growing, shrinking, or changing shape, and what that means for positioning
* Building an AI-resilient career - skills, signals, and portfolios that hold their value
* Spotting fake jobs, scam recruiters, and AI-generated postings
* Practical workflows and tools that are actually worth using

After these sessions we typically grab dinner nearby if you want to keep the conversation going and connect with other professionals.

title: Cosmologies
location: Te Uru Waitākere Contemporary Gallery, 420 Titirangi Road, Titirangi, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Cosmologies brings together the work of Nikau Hindin and Naminapu Maymuru-White into an exhibition that generates dialogue shaped by the night sky.
Across Indigenous knowledge systems celestial bodies are not distant matter but living presences, they are repositories of law, memory, navigation, spirit energy and ecological care. Stars orient seasonal cycles and kinship structures, binding people to land, sea and sky. In this exhibition, cosmology is not metaphor but method: a way of mapping relations across generations and more-than-human worlds. A way to locate our own position in this world and in this life. Working with aute (barkcloth) and bark painting respectively, both artists translate lived astronomical knowledge into contemporary abstraction while remaining grounded in ancestral responsibility.
Emerging from sustained engagement with Te Ao Māori, specifically cosmological knowledge, Hindin’s work centres on the reinvigoration of traditional cultural practices. Inscribing natural pigments onto aute, made from paper mulberry by the artist, she charts stellar movements in alignment with the maramataka, the Māori lunar calendar. Lines extend across the cloth as diagrams of time, translating navigational knowledge into material form. The compositions function as both star maps and environmental compasses, encoding rising and setting points of stars along the horizon. Hindin reactivates systems of orientation, but also techniques disrupted by colonial imposition. Mapping here is an act of remembering - locating knowledge in the body, in material and in time.
Grounded in Yolŋu cosmology, particularily the Milŋiyawuy - the river of stars known in Western astronomy as the Milky Way - Maymuru-White’s practice renders the night sky as a living lineage-based current. Using black and white ochres on bark, she renders dense, rhythmic constellations and flowing star rivers that carry tribal narratives of origin, journey and obligation. title: Pacific Dance Festival
location: Auckland
description:
Pacific Dance Festival returns this June with a powerful celebration of contemporary Pacific identity in Aotearoa, bringing together artists from across the Moana in an expanded 2026 programme.
Returning to South Auckland, the cultural heart of the Pacific diaspora, the festival finds home in the Māngere Arts Centre - Ngā Tohu o Uenuku, Te Oro Music and Arts Centre in Glen Innes and Toi Tū - Studio One Toi Tū in Auckland Central.
Festival Director Iosefa Enari MNZM says: “Pacific Dance Festival 2026 is a declaration of who we are now - a diverse, global, future-focused Pacific. Our artists are innovators, storytellers and cultural leaders. This year we honour the full Moana, from Micronesia to Polynesia, and we do it from South Auckland - the home of Pacific creativity.”
The 2026 programme brings together artists from Wallis & Futuna (ʻUvea), Kiribati, Rotuma, Samoa, Aotearoa, and the Indigenous Pacific diaspora of Te Whanganui-a-Tara. The festival spans traditional, contemporary and street-based practice, showcasing established, emerging, and youth voices.
Festival highlights:
CALL TO WALLIS - Justin Haiu 5 - 6 June | Māngere Arts Centre
A powerful contemporary work honouring ʻUvean identity and ancestral memory.
MOANA SHOWCASE 9 June | Māngere Arts Centre
Aotearoa’s leading dance institutions present new Pacific works.
TRIPLE BILL: Kamataga × In the Fale × Vignette of the Frigate 11 June | Māngere Arts Centre
Three contemporary works exploring identity, beginnings, Melanesian womanhood, and Pacific migration.
MAREWEN KIRIBATI YOUTH GROUP - Full Show 2 June | Māngere Arts Centre
A vibrant celebration of Kiribati culture and youth leadership.
SHIFTING CENTRE - THE CIRCLE 15 - 16 June | Māngere Arts Centre
Explosive contemporary dance from Wellington’s Indigenous collective.
SAMOAN LANGUAGE WEEK WORKSHOPS Early June | Toi Tū & Te Oro
Community movement workshops celebrating Gagana Samoa.

title: No Other Land (2024) Palestine
location: 2 Freyberg Place, Auckland
description:
No Other Land is a documentary/drama about life in Palestine. This is the second in our films about Palestine. The intention here is to open up discussion based on the power of cinema to portray the lives of ordinary people in their struggles in the face of oppressive forces.

We know the debate about whether the films of Leni Riefenstahl in WW2 were propaganda or art. Great cinema paints a picture of people whose lives become real in front of our eyes. We are forced to make decisions as to to whom we relate and what we will do.

"A combination of hand-held footage and intimate scenes of ordinary Palestinian life among extraordinary instability are woven together at an artful pace. Not one of the 95 minutes feels wasted. Given the work that Adra and Abraham do during years of filming to record and share the truth, this is a film that asks, both out-loud and implicitly: if people knew, would things change? *No Other Land* is both an invitation and a wero, a generous offering that demands to be seen and discussed. — Nadia Abu-Shanab." (reviewer for the NZ International Film Festival)

title: A Man For All Seasons
location:
Titirangi Theatre - Lopdell House, 418 Titirangi Road, Titirangi, Auckland
, Auckland
description:
Tudor England, the 1530s. The court of King Henry VIII hums with intrigue and quiet menace. Power shifts behind closed doors. Alliances are made and unmade in an instant. In this world, ambition is currency and a single misstep can have catastrophic consequences.
Robert Bolt’s A Man for All Seasons tells the true story of Sir Thomas More, a man known for his integrity, caught in a time of political and religious upheaval. As the King demands loyalty at any cost, More is forced to choose between serving his monarch and staying true to his conscience.
Tense, intelligent and still sharply relevant for audiences today, this enduring drama asks what it really costs to stand by your principles when silence is no longer safe.

It is a free, safe space for babies, toddlers, preschoolers, and their grown-ups. Come along to play and connect with each other and other families.
